titleStmt.title: History of the Zhou Dynasty · Shang 商

div.head: c. 1260 BC
div.p: After Pan Geng's death his younger brothers Xiao Xin and Xiao Yi succeeded in turn; by the accession of Xiao Yi's son Wu Ding, the Middle Shang culture had formally passed into Yinxu Phase I.

The main body of the Zhukaigou people left the Ordos region and moved south into northern Shaanxi, exerting a certain influence on the Shang culture of the Guanzhong region; the characteristic Zhukaigou vessel, the snake-pattern li, has been unearthed at Shang-culture sites such as Beicun in Yao County and Yijiabu in Fufeng. Some scholars take them to be the Fang.

During Wu Ding's reign a series of campaigns was also made against the fang states and tribes of the Wei River valley; since the Middle Shang the Shang culture of Guanzhong had taken on an ever more local character, and Wu Ding's dispatch of armies against the Quanfang may be an epitome of the Shang court's attempt to tighten its hold on the western lands once more.

The "Zhoufang" of the oracle-bone inscriptions is generally taken to be the Zhou people who later founded the Zhou dynasty. In the earlier part of King Wu Ding's reign, corresponding in archaeological terms to Yinxu Phase I, the Zhengjiapo culture appeared in the valley of the Qishui River, its sites interspersed with those of the Jingdang-type Shang culture of the Zhouyuan region. At the same time the Sunjia type appeared around Binzhou and Xunyi, close in its cultural character to the Zhengjiapo culture; both have been regarded by scholars as Proto-Zhou culture.
